name: capacity-plan
prompt:
This depot model needs to become a capacity plan. There are three things to do, and the later ones depend on the earlier ones, so work out the order before you start editing.

1. COSTING BUG. `handling_rate` is meant to be charged per unit of load on a route, not once per route. Fix `cost_of` so handling scales with the route's load. Every number below depends on this, so do it first.

2. HEAVY ROUTES. Add a `heavy_cutoff` binding and a `heavy` binding holding the routes whose load is strictly greater than the cutoff. Choose the SMALLEST whole-number cutoff for which fewer than 100 routes count as heavy. Loads run from 1 to 40. You cannot read this off the source -- the routes are generated -- so you will have to try a cutoff, see how many routes come back, and adjust.

3. CHEAPEST REGION. Regions are numbered 0 to 4. Add whatever bindings you need to work out the total cost of each region's routes, and which region is cheapest overall. `in_region` and `costs_of` already exist; build on them rather than re-filtering from scratch.

Finally, change the program's last expression to a three-part tuple:

    (total_cost, heavy_count, cheapest_region)

where `heavy_count` is how many routes are heavy and `cheapest_region` is the region number.

HOW TO WORK. You do not see the program's value while you are part-way through a turn -- you only find out after you stop. So when you need to know a number (the heavy count for a given cutoff, or a region's total), either inspect it with your tools or end your turn and you will be told what the program currently evaluates to. Changing a value several times in a row without looking at any of the results tells you nothing. Build the answer up in stages and check as you go.

When the tuple is right, say DONE and stop.
expectation:
The combined task, and the largest program in the set (~55 lines, ~278ms per evaluation). It is deliberately a mixture rather than a clean case, so it should land BETWEEN add-metrics and fix-middle rather than beating either.

It exercises all three edit locations in one trace: a middle-of-pipeline fix to `cost_of` (step 1) which invalidates every cost downstream but leaves the expensive `routes` binding cached; an empirical search over `heavy_cutoff` (step 2) which is pure iterate-and-retry with everything above it stable; and additive bindings for the per-region analysis (step 3) which is the best case. It also requires planning -- the sub-goals are ordered by dependency, and the prompt says so without giving the order away for free.

NOTE: `goal` is an oracle the agent never sees. Expected answer is (140046, 98, 4): total cost 140046 once handling scales with load, 98 heavy routes at cutoff 30 (the smallest cutoff giving fewer than 100), and region 4 cheapest at 27324. There is no cutoff giving exactly 100 heavy routes, which is why the target is phrased as a threshold rather than a percentage.

This is the task most likely to produce a messy trace, because it is the one the agent is most likely to get partly wrong. A partial or failed attempt is still a usable measurement so long as the no-op audit stays clean -- but read the audit and the goal verdict before quoting a number from it.
